answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a costly, verifiable history: reputation is earned only through attested work over time, like timber seasoning slowly instead of appearing overnight. New identities climb a trellis of limited trust — small tasks, peer review, and slashable stake — so spawning a thousand sock puppets buys no influence. Even a whisper of coordinated fakery shows up when fresh accounts share timing, wording, or funding trails, letting the network prune them before they vote or earn.
